h1: The 8 Best Small Dehumidifiers Under $150 for Bedrooms, Closets and RVs, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 8 compact dehumidifiers under $150 for bedrooms, closets and RVs, compared on tank size, coverage, noise and auto shut-off.
summary: The 1657mL, 58 oz Small Dehumidifier rated for 230 square feet is the dehumidifier to buy under $150 if you want the largest tank and a defrost safeguard, and the OWAAE is the quiet bedroom pick with auto shut-off and a sleep mode. The NineSky, NeedDuck and TABYIK units are lighter-duty options, and none of these replaces a full-size basement unit.
intro: The honest truth about a dehumidifier under $150 is that it is not the machine you picture when someone says dehumidifier. These are compact units, the size of a toaster or a small speaker, built for a closet, a bathroom, a bedroom or an RV. A full-size compressor unit that pulls gallons of water a day from a damp basement costs more and weighs far more. Buy a mini unit for a mini job, and a big one for a basement.

We reviewed eight compact dehumidifiers from their listings, which are thin on numbers: many give tank sizes and marketing copy but omit pints-per-day ratings. We ranked them on tank capacity, stated coverage area, noise and safety features, and note the gaps rather than guess. Price buckets replace exact prices, and no figures here come from testing.

products.name: Dehumidifier 1657ML 58OZ Small Dehumidifier for Home 230 Ft² Safety
products.verdict: A 1657mL tank, a stated 230 square foot range, defrost protection and three quiet modes.
products.description:
This small dehumidifier has a 1657mL (58 oz) water tank, a stated coverage of 230 square feet, defrosting and safety protection, and three setting modes with quiet operation. It sits in the $25 to $50 bracket.

It comes first because it is the only unit here that states a coverage area, and the tank is the largest in the group. A bigger tank means fewer trips to the sink and fewer overflow scares. The defrost feature matters because small cooling-based units can ice up in cool rooms, and a protection mode that handles it keeps the machine working. The three modes let you drop to a lower setting at night.

Buy it if you have a bedroom or office up to 230 square feet. Do not expect it to dry a basement.
cons: Not for basements or large rooms
Daily removal rate is not given
products.idealFor: Bedrooms and offices up to 230 sq ft.
products.skipIf: You need to dry a whole basement.

products.name: OWAAE Dehumidifier for Home with Auto Shutoff Sleep Mode
products.verdict: Auto shut-off, a sleep mode and a design for bedrooms, bathrooms and enclosed spaces.
products.description:
The OWAAE is a dehumidifier for home use with an auto shut-off and a sleep mode, described as ultra-quiet for bedrooms and nighttime and optimized for bathrooms and enclosed spaces. It sits in the $50 to $100 bracket.

Its focus on quiet and unattended running is why it ranks high. In a bedroom, noise is the first complaint with any dehumidifier, and a sleep mode reduces output at night. Auto shut-off stops the unit when the tank is full, which prevents overflow and unnecessary running. The tank volume is not stated, so you cannot compare its holding capacity, and it costs more than the leader.

Buy it if the dehumidifier will run while you sleep. Skip it if you want a stated coverage area and a large tank.
pros: Auto shut-off when the tank is full
products.idealFor: Bedrooms where noise is the main worry.
products.skipIf: You want a stated coverage area.

products.name: NineSky Dehumidifiers for Home
products.verdict: A quiet, high-efficiency unit with smart auto shut-off for removing dampness at home.
products.description:
The NineSky is a compact dehumidifier pitched as quiet and high efficiency, with smart auto shut-off protection, for removing dampness at home. It falls in the $50 to $100 bracket.

The auto shut-off is the feature to value, since a unit left running while you are out can overflow if it lacks one. The listing talks of a next-generation approach but never names the cooling method, the tank volume or a daily removal rate, so its claims of efficiency cannot be checked. It ranks third because the safety feature is real while the rest is marketing language.

Buy it if you want a small, quiet unit for a bathroom or closet. Ask the seller for tank size and coverage before you decide.
products.idealFor: Bathrooms and closets needing a quiet unit.

products.name: NeedDuck Dehumidifier for Home Small Quiet Dehumidifiers for 44OZ Water Tank
products.verdict: A compact quiet unit with a 44 oz tank and built-in safety, in the $25 to $50 bracket.
products.description:
The NeedDuck is a small, quiet dehumidifier with a 44 oz water tank and built-in safety and convenience features. It falls in the $25 to $50 bracket.

The listing is candid that it is not a high-power machine focused on rapid moisture removal, which sets realistic expectations. A 44 oz tank holds less than the leader but more than the 35 oz units. It suits closets, small bathrooms and desks where gentle, steady drying is enough. It ranks fourth because the coverage and daily removal figures are not given.

Buy it if you want to keep spending low and the space is small. Skip it if you expect to fight a serious damp problem.
pros: 44 oz tank beats the 35 oz units
products.idealFor: Closets and small bathrooms on a budget.
products.skipIf: You have a serious damp problem.

products.name: TABYIK 35 OZ Dehumidifier for Bedroom RV
products.verdict: A 35 oz portable dehumidifier for bedrooms and RVs, in the $25 to $50 range.
products.description:
The TABYIK is a 35 oz portable dehumidifier aimed at bedrooms and RVs, with a compact size and a tank that signals when it is 700 to 800 mL full. It sits in the $25 to $50 bracket.

Its size is its identity. A compact unit fits on a shelf or a RV counter, and the full-tank indicator tells you when to empty it. The 35 oz capacity means frequent emptying in a damp room, and the listing is vague on coverage and removal rate. It ranks fifth because it is a smaller version of what the leaders offer.

Buy it for a small space, a camper or a closet. Plan on emptying the tank daily during humid weather.
products.skipIf: You want to empty it less often.

products.name: ToLife Dehumidifier
products.verdict: A dehumidifier with a powerful mode and seven color ambient lighting options.
products.description:
The ToLife is marketed as a high-efficiency dehumidifier with a powerful mode and seven color options for ambient lighting. It sits in the $50 to $100 bracket.

The lighting is a bedroom feature, a soft glow that some people like as a night light and others find distracting. The powerful mode is the performance claim, but no tank size, coverage area or removal rate appears in the listing, so it is hard to see what the extra money buys. It ranks sixth because style features are doing more of the selling than specs.

Buy it if the ambient light appeals to you and the room is small. Turn the lights off if you sleep in the same room.
products.idealFor: Small rooms where a night light is welcome.
products.skipIf: You want specs more than style.

products.name: BEDRED Dehumidifier
products.verdict: A semiconductor, thermoelectric-cooling unit with auto shut-off and 7-color ambient light.
products.description:
The BEDRED uses semiconductor thermoelectric cooling to remove moisture, with intelligent auto shut-off and a 7-color ambient light. It falls in the $50 to $100 bracket.

It stands out for naming its technology. Thermoelectric units have no compressor, so they are quiet and light, and they work best in small, warm, humid spaces such as a bathroom or closet. They are less effective in cool rooms, where they remove far less water. The price is high for what this method can do, and the listing states no tank size.

Buy it if you want a silent unit for a small warm space. Skip it for a cool basement or a large room.
products.skipIf: The room is cool or large.

products.name: TABYIK 35 OZ Dehumidifier for Bedroom RV (High efficient dehumidifiers)
products.verdict: A second TABYIK 35 oz listing with the same small tank and 700 to 800 mL fill alert.
products.description:
This TABYIK listing mirrors the other: a 35 oz portable dehumidifier for bedrooms and RVs, with a tank that signals at 700 to 800 mL. It costs very little.

It ranks last because it offers nothing that the sibling listing does not, and the high efficient label is a marketing phrase, not a measured claim. Compare prices on the two listings and buy whichever is cheaper or in stock. The small tank and brief spec sheet are the same.

Buy it if it is available when the other is not. Otherwise choose the NeedDuck, which adds tank size and safety detail for the same bracket.
products.idealFor: A backup source for the same small unit.

methodology.title: Tank size
methodology.description: We compared tanks of 35 oz, 44 oz and 58 oz (1657mL), since they decide how often you must empty the unit.

methodology.title: Stated coverage

methodology.title: Safety features
methodology.description: Auto shut-off, defrost protection and full-tank indicators were counted because unattended units can overflow.

methodology.title: Noise and mode options
methodology.description: Sleep modes and quiet-operation claims were weighed for bedroom use, with stated claims discounted as seller figures.

methodology.title: Value
methodology.description: Feature depth was set against the $25 to $50 and $50 to $100 brackets, all well under the $150 limit.

whatMatters.detail: A small tank fills quickly in a damp room. 35 oz is a minimum, 44 oz is workable, and 58 oz is generous for this class. Check the tank size in the title or spec list, and expect to empty it daily in humid weather.

A mini dehumidifier is built for a closet, a bathroom or a small bedroom. One listing states 230 square feet, which is a realistic ceiling. For a living room or a basement, you need a compressor model.

Thermoelectric units are silent and light but weak in cool rooms. Compressor units remove more water but are louder and costlier. Listings often skip this detail, so treat a missing explanation as a sign of a basic thermoelectric unit.
Auto shut-off stops the unit when the tank is full, and defrost protection helps in cool rooms. Both prevent damage and mess. Look for them in the feature list, as on the 1657mL unit and the NineSky.
Bedroom units should be quiet, and ambient lights can disturb sleep. Look for a sleep mode or a way to switch lights off. Noise ratings are seller claims, so favor units with documented modes.

faq.q: Can a dehumidifier under $150 dry a basement?
faq.a: Not reliably. These are compact units for closets, bathrooms and bedrooms. A basement needs a compressor dehumidifier rated in pints per day, which generally costs more than $150.

faq.q: What is the biggest mistake when buying a small dehumidifier?
faq.a: Buying one for a room that is too big. A unit rated for 230 square feet struggles in a 600 square foot space. Match the stated coverage to the room, or buy a larger machine.

faq.q: Is the 1657mL model worth it over a TABYIK?
faq.a: Yes, for most rooms. The tank holds nearly twice as much as a 35 oz unit, it states a coverage area, and it has defrost protection. The TABYIK is cheaper but fills faster.

faq.q: How do I set one up?
faq.a: Place it on a flat surface with space around the vents, plug it in, pick a mode and empty the tank when it fills. Keep doors and windows closed so it treats the same air.

faq.q: How do I keep it from smelling?
faq.a: Empty the tank after each full cycle, rinse it with mild soap, and dry the inside. Standing water in a tank breeds odors and mold quickly, so do not leave it full for days.

faq.q: Do thermoelectric dehumidifiers work in cold rooms?
faq.a: They work poorly. Thermoelectric cooling depends on a temperature difference, so output falls in cool rooms. For a cold basement, a compressor model with defrost is a better choice.

finalTake: For a bedroom or small office, the 1657mL Small Dehumidifier rated for 230 square feet is the best buy under $150, with the biggest tank and defrost protection. The OWAAE is the quiet pick for sleeping spaces, the NeedDuck is a sensible low-cost closet unit, and the TABYIK models suit RVs. Measure the room first, because a mini unit only wins in a small space.
